context.title: Five Nations Under Judgment
context.summary: Short oracles address Ammon, which seized Israelite land; Edom, proud in its rocky heights; Damascus, 'the city of my joy'; the desert tribes of Kedar and Hazor; and distant Elam. Several end with a surprising promise of restoration.
context.background: Ammon's capital, Rabbah (v. 2), is modern Amman, Jordan; Ammon had moved into the land of Gad east of the Jordan after Assyria deported Israelites (v. 1). Verses 9–10 and 14–16 closely parallel Obadiah 1–6. Elam (vv. 34–39) lay east of Babylon in what is now southwestern Iran; its city Susa later became a Persian royal capital.

customs.note: A warning to hide in caves and remote places, out of the invader's reach (also v. 8).

watchFor: Edom's nest 'as high as the eagle' (v. 16) echoes Obadiah 1:4.
The 'lion from the swelling of Jordan' (v. 19) is used again of Babylon in 50:44.

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18).

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.summary: The king of Syria whom Asa, king of Judah, employed to invade Israel (1 Kings 15:18).

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Kedar
people.summary: Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13).

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18).

places.name: Gad

places.name: Rabbah
places.summary: “Rabbath of the children of Ammon,” the chief city of the Ammonites, among the eastern hills, some 20 miles east of the Jordan, on the southern of the two streams which united with the Jabbok.

places.name: Ai
places.summary: A city in the Ammonite territory (Jer. 49:3).

places.name: Heshbon
places.summary: Intelligence, a city ruled over by Sihon, king of the Amorites (Josh. 3:10; 13:17). It was taken by Moses (Num. 21:23-26), and became afterwards a Levitical city (Josh. 21:39) in the tribe of Reuben (Num. 32:37).

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Teman
places.summary: A place in Southern Idumea, the land of “the sons of the east,” frequently mentioned in the Old Testament. It was noted for the wisdom of its inhabitants (Amos 1:12; Obad. 1:8; Jer. 49:7; Ezek. 25:13).

places.name: Dedan
places.summary: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-%27Ula

places.name: Esau
places.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

places.name: Bozrah
places.summary: The city of Jobab, one of the early Edomite kings (Gen. 36:33). This place is mentioned by the prophets in later times (Isa. 34:6; Jer. 49:13; Amos 1:12; Micah 2:12).

places.name: Gomorrah
places.summary: Submersion, one of the five cities of the plain of Siddim which were destroyed by fire (Gen. 10:19; 13:10; 19:24, 28). These cities probably stood close together, and were near the northern extremity of what is now the Dead Sea.

places.name: Sodom
places.summary: Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Red sea
places.summary: The sea so called extends along the west coast of Arabia for about 1,400 miles, and separates Asia from Africa. It is connected with the Indian Ocean, of which it is an arm, by the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb.

places.name: Arpad
places.summary: (Isa. 10:9; 36:19; 37:13), also Arphad, support, a Syrian city near Hamath, along with which it is invariably mentioned (2 Kings 19:13; 18:34; Isa. 10:9), and Damascus (Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Damascus
places.summary: Activity, the most ancient of Oriental cities; the capital of Syria (Isa. 7:8; 17:3); situated about 133 miles to the north of Jerusalem.

places.name: Hamath
places.summary: Fortress, the capital of one of the kingdoms of Upper Syria of the same name, on the Orontes, in the valley of Lebanon, at the northern boundary of Palestine (Num. 13:21; 34:8), at the foot of Hermon (Josh. 13:5) towards Damascus (Zech. 9:2; Jer. 49:23).

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

places.name: Hazor
places.summary: A district in Arabia (Jer. 49:28-33), supposed by some to be Jetor, i.e., Ituraea.

places.name: Kedar
places.summary: Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13).

places.name: Elam
places.summary: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles.

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
